FAQ

Common questions

Are the degrees and certificates recognised?

Yes. Every program is delivered directly by the partner institution named on its course card, so the degree or certificate carries that institution’s own recognition.

What documents are required?

Typically academic transcripts, a government ID, an updated resume, and any work-experience letters relevant to your chosen program’s eligibility. Your counsellor confirms the exact list for that program.

Is an entrance exam required?

It depends on the program and institution — many executive and working-professional tracks waive standardised entrance exams in favour of work experience and academic background.

Are scholarships / EMI options available?

Instalment (EMI) options are available on many programs, and some qualify for scholarships or financing support. Ask your counsellor which apply to your shortlisted program.

Are the programs valid in India and internationally?

Each program’s validity follows the accreditation of its awarding institution. Your counsellor can confirm recognition for your specific country or employer before you apply.

What is the minimum work experience required?

This varies by program — some certificates accept fresh Bachelor’s graduates, while executive and doctorate programs typically require 3–8+ years of experience. Check the Eligibility line on each course card.

Who can apply?

Working professionals and graduates who meet a program’s stated eligibility — typically a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, sometimes with a minimum number of years of work experience.

How long does each program take?

Program duration is shown on every course card — certificates typically run 4–7 months, master’s and executive programs 13–18 months, and doctorate programs 24–36 months.

Are the programs online?

Yes — with a choice of Online, Offline, or Any mode. You can select your preferred mode when you apply.

How does admission work?

Submit your details, complete an eligibility assessment, speak with a counsellor, then complete your admission — see How It Works below for the full four-step process.

Not Sure Which Program Is Right For You?
